SHA-256:
17df34ca64cc60e107f0c214db4729c54a514df4e32de5bc1b8b7b7c5a805a56

SceneIO fetches that immutable archive at configure time and compiles only:
- cpp/lazperf/*.cpp
- cpp/lazperf/detail/*.cpp

Upstream's shared library, tools, examples, tests, benchmarks, install rules,
and downloaded test data are not configured.

Local correctness patch:
- cpp/lazperf/streams.hpp MemoryStream::getByte checks idx against buf.size()
  and throws lazperf::error on exhaustion before indexing. Upstream format-1.4
  decoders copy bounded layer bytes into this vector, so the check converts a
  corrupt arithmetic layer's over-read into the same clean codec error as an
  exhausted outer callback. CMake applies an exact idempotent replacement and
  fails if the pinned target changes.
- cpp/lazperf/decompressor.hpp routes full-range predictor addition through the
  shared modulo-2^32 helper, computes bounded predictor/corrector arithmetic in
  int64 in both the normal and optional COMPRESS_ONLY_K decoder branches, and
  rejects a malformed k=31 corrector that cannot fit int32. This preserves
  valid LASzip arithmetic while making corrupted layered streams raise
  lazperf::error instead of executing signed-overflow behavior. CMake migrates
  the earlier inline form, accepts exactly one known include/predictor state,
  requires exactly two original or two patched corrector blocks, writes the
  fetched header only when its content changes, and fails if the pinned targets
  change. Off-by-default native correctness targets compile the normal and
  COMPRESS_ONLY_K branches in separate executables and drive controlled k=31
  symbols to the exact range rejection.
- cpp/lazperf/utils.hpp defines the LAS modulo-2^32 conversion once;
  compressor.hpp, decompressor.hpp, detail/field_point10.cpp,
  detail/field_point14.cpp, and detail/field_xyz.hpp use it for full-range
  coordinate differences and reconstruction. The compressor also derives an
  INT32_MIN magnitude without signed negation, performs its bounded corrector
  fold in int64, and uses an unsigned high-bit shift. These changes preserve
  the LASzip wrap convention for valid INT32_MIN/INT32_MAX transitions on both
  legacy and layered point formats. CMake applies each replacement exactly
  once and the native arithmetic target checks the wrap boundaries directly.

The wrapper also validates container extents and supplies bounded callbacks
before calling the codec.
